covers.description: the system cover and the drive cage cover on top, and the optional security bezel on the front. The bezel is DRAWN FITTED, as on the R740xd and R660: it is `mounts`, so the viewer takes it off to show the drives, and `for:` names what it covers.

drives.description: the 2.5 inch front bays, numbered as the strip under the carriers prints them (the 32 bay front's lower row continues 16-31)

drives-e3s.description: the EDSFF E3.S front bays, sixteen standing carriers numbered left to right as ISM figure 27 gives them (0-15, or 8-23 after the 2.5 inch bank)

attrs.redundancy-note: R960 technical guide, thermal features: "The R960 allows N+1 fan redundancy, allowing continuous operation with one fan failure in the system."

fans.description: the six dual-rotor fan modules in the fan cage, numbered 1 to 6 as the cage prints them, left to right as the front faces you

interior.description: the system board, the processor expansion module, the fan cage, the air shrouds and the support bar

lom-card.description: the LOM card position, held as a card and not its two ports (the ports are the card's own)

marks.description: printed marks seated as parts - the VGA symbol

memory.description: the 32 DDR5 slots of the system board, A1-A16 for processor 1 and B1-B16 for processor 2, named as ISM figure 95 prints them, seen from above with the rear at the top. The other 32 are `memory-expansion`

memory-expansion.description: the 32 DDR5 slots of the processor expansion module, C1-C16 for processor 3 and D1-D16 for processor 4, as ISM figure 96 prints them. A group of their own because the PEM stands over the system board: each of its sockets has a twin under it at the same plan position

panels.description: the left control panel, a field-replaceable module in the left ear

ports.description: the front VGA, the USB-A and the iDRAC Direct micro-AB USB

processors.description: the four processor heatsinks - CPU 1 and CPU 3 on the right as the front faces you, CPU 2 and CPU 4 on the left (CPU 3 and 4 on the processor expansion module)

attrs.redundancy-note: R960 ISM and technical guide: four AC or DC power supply units with 2+2 redundancy (ISM "System overview"; technical guide "Power supply units": up to four AC supplies with 2+2 redundancy, autosensing and auto switching).

psus.description: the four 86 mm supply bays, PSU 3 over PSU 1 at the left and PSU 4 over PSU 2 at the right as the rear faces you

rear-io.description: the rear I/O board position - the board carries the ID button, the iDRAC port, two USB and the VGA, which are its own ports

risers.description: the expansion card riser positions, numbered as Dell numbers them (1, 2, 3 and 4). `service` and not `traffic`, as on the R740xd: the group holds the riser, and the cards live in the riser's own slot bays, numbered as ISM table 88 numbers them.

tags.description: the slide-out Express Service Tag under the right-hand drives

name: r960

bezel.note: DRAWN FITTED, as on the R740xd and R660, and taken off in the viewer: the optional security bezel (dell/r960-bezel@1) covers the body between the ears, and `for:` names the bays and parts behind it. Its openings are holes, so the drives show through. MEASURED from Dell's R960 service model, working/intake/dell/3d-models/r960.glb: `R960_ FrontBezel` in the `Main Assembly` node, 430.8 x 168.5 at front-face (25.5, 2.7), its plate's 42 openings found by decoding the mesh (large hexagons in a staggered grid, 38.5 by 44.45 apart) and its release button. The model's bezel is the LCD bezel and the security bezel's own shape is not in it; the ISM says the mesh is the same (figure 34), and the lock's place is a guess (see `security-bezel-shape-estimated`). The LCD bezel is not modelled.

chassis.note: datasheet - ISM table 7 (chassis dimensions, figure 32): Xb 444.0 is the body BETWEEN THE EARS and Xa 482.0 across them, Y 174.3 the height, Za 36 mm with the bezel and 22 mm without it (ear plane to the front), Zb 844.74 ear to rear wall and Zc 847.195 ear to PSU handle. DEPTH 866.74 IS THE FRONT FACE TO THE REAR WALL: the 22 mm the ears sit behind the front face without the bezel plus Zb, as the R660's is derived. It agrees with the spec sheet's 869.195 without the bezel and 883.195 with it, which are Za + Zc (22 + 847.195 and 36 + 847.195): they reach the PSU handles, 2.455 further than the rear wall. The technical guide's table 2 prints the same 883.195 and 869.195 for the R960 and, beside them, 441.16 wide and 877.84 / 865.9 deep: THOSE ARE THE PREVIOUS-GENERATION R940xa's COLUMN of the same table, not the R960's, which the guide's own chassis table (Xb 444 mm) and ISM table 7 confirm. A converted copy that merged the two columns reads 441.16; the ISM governs.

drive-bays.note: photo-measured - the 2.5 inch bays are columns of 17.4 mm on the figures' own pitch (17.75 mm in the left bank, 17.28 in the middle and right banks of figures 2 and 3, 17.7 across figure 1), each 76.2 tall: the carriers' orange release buttons were found by colour and give each column's centre, and the carrier sits centred in it. The carrier is common/drive-carrier-25@2, standing up, as the R740xd seats it. The three banks of figure 2 do not share a pitch; it is drawn as measured, per bank.

drive-default.note: EVERY BAY DEFAULTS TO A BLANK, as on the R660 and R740xd: Dell publishes no default drive count, and the ISM requires blanks in every empty slot for cooling. A populated machine is a configuration.

drive-numbering.note: photo-measured - a number strip runs under the upper row of drives on figures 1 to 3, 5 and 6 and prints the bay numbers: 0-7 in the left bank and 8-15 in the right on the 16 and 32 bay fronts, 0-23 across the 24 bay front, with CPU tags between pairs (CPU4 between 2 and 3, CPU2 between 8 and 9, CPU1 between 14 and 15, CPU3 between 20 and 21) and an NVMe tag at the left. The 32-bay front prints 0-15 only, on the strip between its two rows: the lower row's 16 to 31 are NOT PRINTED on the figure, and it is numbered 16-31 by continuing the sequence (see the lower-row gap).

e3s.note: photo-measured - ISM figures 5 and 6: sixteen EDSFF E3.S carriers standing side by side in the right of the upper band, found by the SSD legend printed down each carrier on a 34.87 px (10.51 mm) pitch from 290.3 mm across; the carrier is dell/e3s-carrier@1 (the R660's, the same Dell part) turned 90 so its orange chevrons are at the top as the figures show. THE E3.S NUMBERS ARE NOT PRINTED on either figure (the strip under the block carries no digits); the bays are numbered from ISM figure 27, the service label (a drive number, then "Bay 1 (0-7)", "Bay 2 (8-15)"): 0-15 left to right on the 16 E3.S front and, because the 2.5 inch bank is bay 1 (0-7), 8-23 on the 8 + 16 front.

front-face.note: THE EARS CARRY THE CONTROL PANELS, SO THEY ARE DRAWN - the R740xd's and R660's reasoning: the left control panel (ISM figure 7) sits in the left ear outboard of the drives and the right panel (power, USB, iDRAC Direct, ISM figure 9) and the VGA in the right. The front is therefore the 482.0 rack face (ISM Xa), 174.3 tall.

fronts.note: SIX FRONTS, EACH ITS OWN VIEW bound by `configurations.<name>.views`, as the R660's and R740xd's are: ISM figure 1 (32 x 2.5 inch, `front-sff32`), 2 (24 x 2.5 inch, `front-sff24`), 3 (16 x 2.5 inch, `front`), 4 (8 x 2.5 inch, `front-sff8`), 5 (16 x EDSFF E3.S, `front-e3s16`) and 6 (8 x 2.5 inch with 16 x EDSFF E3.S, `front-sff8-e3s16`). The ISM's "16 x 2.5 inch SAS/SATA + 8 x 2.5 inch NVMe" is a backplane mix on the 24 bay face (ISM table 70 and the cabling tables 75, 76), not a seventh front; the technical guide's "32 x 2.5 inch (Smart Flow)" caption is figure 1. The ISM names no front without a backplane.

gate-1.note: Gate 1 passed. ISM figures 1 to 6 are 1623 x 809 px photographs (300 ppi). Measured by non-white extent, the ear-to-ear width of figures 2 to 6 is 1599 px and the height 581 px: 3.3175 px/mm across the 482.0 face and 3.333 px/mm down the 174.3 height, 0.5% apart, so they are orthographic enough to take positions from. Figure 1 (32 bays) is a differently scaled copy: 1590 x 578 px, 3.299 and 3.316 px/mm, 0.5% apart. Every front position here is read off them at those scales.

rear.note: photo-measured - ISM figure 10, the rear view (a 1565 x 807 photograph), which is riser configuration 2 (R1B + R2 + R3B + R4B) with four 2800 W supplies. Body 23..1521 px across (444 mm, 3.374 px/mm) and 110..691 down (174.3, 3.333 px/mm): 1.2% apart, so positions are good to about a millimetre. The rear face is the 444 body, not the rack face. The technical guide's figures 7 and 8 (600 ppi, 5% out between axes: read for shape only) show configurations 0 and 1: no riser 2 (a plate across its band), and in configuration 0 a vented plate where riser 3 would be.

rear-boss-lom-io.note: photo-measured - the BOSS-N1 module on riser 1's side at 131.3, 10.4 (its two M.2 carriers, 480 GB, orange tab at the bottom of carrier 0 and the top of carrier 1: the R660's dell/boss-n1-module-1u@1, the same part); the LOM window at 118.8..160.6 and the OCP card at 171.4..243.2 (71.8 wide, the library's OCP bay), LOM and OCP in the R660's left-to-right order; the rear I/O board is NOT the R660's (96.4 wide against 85.37 and with its connectors on a different pitch): dell/r960-rear-io-board@1.

rear-power.note: chassis.power is `ac`: every supply this device accepts is an AC supply (100-240 V AC or 240 V DC, hot swap): 1100 and 1400 W in the adapter, 2400 and 2800 W. The 1800 W (C15 cord) and -48 V DC supplies of ISM table 10 are not modelled.

rear-psus.note: photo-measured - four supplies in two stacks: PSU3 above PSU1 at the left (rear x 16.9..103.4) and PSU4 above PSU2 at the right (341.4..427.4), each plate 86.0 wide and about 40.5 tall at y 90.6 and 131.8 (ISM table 5 items 5, 6, 16, 17 and the figure's printed PSU marks). A 60 mm supply stands in this 86 mm bay in a 26 mm adapter (ISM table 11 note); the adapter's side is not stated. The marks (bolt and number) read 3 at the top left, 1 at the lower left, 4 at the top right and 2 at the lower right, as the figure prints them.

rear-risers.note: photo-measured - the riser cages 18.0..122.1 (riser 1), 176.4..280.7 (riser 3) and 317.7..422.9 (riser 4), the riser 2 band 124.2..273.9 under riser 3 and the VGA bracket blank above it; each riser's windows are 20 mm apart. Riser 4's cage prints 1 up, 2 down, 3 down and 4 down at its left (see the gaps: the ISM numbers its slots 10-12) and riser 3's prints 5 up 6 down and 7 up 8 down at its right; the slot numbers on every riser are those of the ISM.

sides-and-bottom.note: estimated - no figure or photograph held shows the bottom or either side; their folded edges and the rail land are plausible shapes at plausible sizes, drawn so the faces are not blank, and marked estimated where drawn.

top.note: measured, where it says so. REAR AT y=0, FRONT AT y=866.74 - the library's plan convention, x left to right as the front faces you (CPU 2 and CPU 4 left, CPU 1 and CPU 3 right). MEASURED from Dell's R960 service model, working/intake/dell/3d-models/r960.glb, read with glbparts.py: the positions come from the un-exploded `Main Assembly` node only (the scene also holds exploded copies under `Extra content`), mapped as plan x = 228.0 - cad x1 (the system cover, cad x -216.0..228.0, is the 444 body) and plan y = 883.94 - cad z1 (the rear wall: the model's chassis front face at cad z 17.2 plus the ISM's 866.74, where its `Hole` cubes stand at 883.6, and the supply handles end 2.56 past it against ISM table 7's 2.455; the handle is modelled at 2.6 mm, the model's figure rounded, 0.145 mm longer than the manual's). What the model gives, each part citing its node: the six fans and the fan cage (`R960_ CoolingFan`), the four heatsinks (`R960_ HeatSink SYS` and `R960_ HeatSink PEM`), the air shroud top cover (`R960_ AirShroudTopCover`) and the shroud under it (`R960_ GPU_AirShroud`), the support bar (`R960_ SupportBar`), the system cover and its latch (`R960_ SystemCover`), the supplies (`R960_ PSU Prefab`), the four risers (`Riser 1B - FL`, `Riser 2`, `Riser 3A - FL`, `Riser 4A - FL`) and the rows of the 64 memory sockets (`Memory Module_SB`, `_PEM`). The model is one build: full-length risers, the GPU shroud and the full-length support bar, where ISM figure 12 is the half-length build; see `top-view-model-vs-ism`. NOT FROM THE MODEL, still read off ISM figures 12 to 15, 95 and 96 (photographs from above, 1.813 px/mm across the 444 body and 1.863 px/mm down, 2.7% apart, with a memory socket drawn 157 long against 133.4 - a 15% stretch down): the two boards' outlines (the model holds them, system board 425.7 x 558.4 at 9.1, 30.0 and PEM 430.4 x 288.1 at 6.8, 264.3, and they are not re-read here), the sockets' x and their names (figures 95, 96: A1-A16 and B1-B16, C1-C16 and D1-D16, named by the labels the figures print) and the drive cage cover. SEATED MODULES PROJECT INTO THIS VIEW through their rear bay's `plan:` - the two upper supplies, the BOSS-N1 module, the OCP card, LOM, rear I/O board and risers - the supplies and risers at the model's positions, the rest mirrored from their rear bays (plan x = 444 - rear x - w). The standing front drives do not project (a standing 2.5 inch drive is 7 mm wide; the library's std/drive-25-plan@1 is a flat drive). NOT YET IN THIS VIEW: the cards, the backplane and the cabling.

vent-plates.note: photo-measured - where no drives fit, the figures show fixed vented plates: one between the two banks of the 16 and 32 bay fronts, two in the upper band of the 8 bay front, two beside the E3.S block and one between the SFF bank and the E3.S block of the 8 + 16 front. The 24 bay front has drives across its whole upper band. Under the upper band three vented plates (the fan wall's grilles) fill the lower band of every front but the 32 bay one, which has a second row of drives there. The plates are read off the figures as rectangles with an inset mesh and are chassis decor; whether Dell's plates are removable blanks is not stated.
